source_text: Μὴ τοίνυν ἀπὸ τῶν παρόντων μόνον περὶ τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ ψηφισώμεθα προνοίας, ἀλλὰ καὶ ἀπὸ τῶν μελλόντων. Τὰ γὰρ παρόντα ἀγών ἐστι καὶ σκάμματα καὶ στάδιον, τὰ δὲ μέλλοντα ἔπαθλα καὶ στέφανοι καὶ βραβεῖα. Ὥσπερ οὖν τὸν ἀθλητὴν, ἐν τῷ σκάμματι καὶ ἱδρῶτι καὶ κόνει καὶ θέρμῃ πολλῇ καὶ πόνοις καὶ ταλαιπωρίαις μάχεσθαι δεῖ, οὕτω καὶ τὸν δίκαιον ἐνταῦθα πολλὰ ὑπομένειν χρὴ καὶ φέρειν ἅπαντα γενναίως, εἴ γε μέλλοι λαμπροὺς ἀπολήψεσθαι τοὺς στεφάνους ἐκεῖ. Εἰ δὲ αἱ τῶν πονηρῶν εὐημερίαι θορυβοῦσί τινας, καὶ ἐπὶ τούτων ἐκεῖνο λογιζέσθωσαν πάλιν, ὅτι, καθάπερ λῃσταὶ καὶ τυμβωρύχοι καὶ ἀνδροφόνοι καὶ οἱ τὴν θάλασσαν πλέοντες πειραταὶ, πρὶν ἢ εἰς τὸ δικαστήριον εἰσελθεῖν, πολλῆς ἀπολαύουσι τρυφῆς, οἰκείαν εὐπορίαν τὰς ἀλλοτρίας ποιούμενοι συμφορὰς, καὶ τὸν ἄδικον κτώμενοι πλοῦτον, καὶ καθ' ἑκάστην μεθύοντες τὴν ἡμέραν· ἐπειδὰν δὲ ὑπὸ ταῖς τοῦ δικαστοῦ γένωνται ψήφοις, πάντων ἐκείνων διδόασι δίκην· οὕτω καὶ οὗτοι οἱ πόρνας ἀγοράζοντες, καὶ τὰς Συβαριτικὰς παρατιθέμενοι τραπέζας, καὶ τὰς ὀφρῦς ἀνασπῶντες, καὶ σοβοῦντες ἐπὶ τῆς ἀγορᾶς, καὶ τοὺς πένητας σπαράττοντες, ὅταν ὁ μονογενὴς Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ παραγένηται μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν ἑαυτοῦ, καὶ ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐκείνου καθίσῃ, καὶ τὴν οἰκουμένην εἰς μέσον παραγάγῃ, γυμνοὶ καὶ πάσης ἔρημοι τῆς φαντασίας εἰσενεχθέντες, καὶ οὐδένα συνήγορον οὐδὲ προστάτην ἔχοντες, χωρὶς συγγνώμης ἁπάσης εἰς τοὺς τοῦ πυρὸς ἀπενεχθήσονται ποταμούς. Μὴ τοίνυν μήτε τούτους μακαρίσῃς διὰ τὴν ἐνταῦθα τρυφὴν, ἀλλὰ δάκρυσον διὰ τὴν μέλλουσαν τιμωρίαν· μηδὲ τὸν δίκαιον ταλανίσῃς διὰ τὴν ἐνταῦθα πενίαν, ἀλλὰ μακάρισον διὰ τὸν μέλλοντα τῶν ἀγαθῶν πλοῦτον, καὶ τὸν περὶ τῆς ἀναστάσεως λόγον ἐν τῇ σαυτοῦ διανοίᾳ ῥίζωσον, ἵνα, κἂν ἀγαθὸς ᾖς καὶ πειράζῃ, δοκιμώτερος γίνῃ, ταῖς μελλούσαις ἐλπίσι προθυμίαν μείζονα προσλαμβάνων· κἂν κακὸς ᾖς, ἀποστῇς τῆς πονηρίας, τῷ φόβῳ τῆς μελλούσης κολάσεως σωφρονέστερον σεαυτὸν κατασκευάζων. βʹ. Διὰ τοῦτο καὶ ὁ Παῦλος συνεχῶς ἡμῖν τὸν περὶ ἀναστάσεως κινεῖ λόγον, καθάπερ οὖν καὶ σήμερον ἠκούσατε αὐτοῦ βοῶντος καὶ λέγοντος· Οἴδαμεν γὰρ, ὅτι ἐὰν ἡ ἐπίγειος ἡμῶν οἰκία τοῦ σκήνους καταλυθῇ, οἰκίαν ἐκ Θεοῦ ἔχομεν ἀχειροποίητον, αἰώνιον, ἐν τοῖς οὐρανοῖς. Μᾶλλον δὲ ἀνωτέρω τὸν λόγον ἀγάγωμεν, καὶ ἴδωμεν πόθεν ἐνέπεσεν εἰς τὸν περὶ ἀναστάσεως λόγον. Οὐ γὰρ ἁπλῶς, οὐδὲ ὡς ἔτυχε, ταύτην συνεχῶς κινεῖ τὴν διδασκαλίαν· ἀλλ' ὁμοῦ τε διδάξαι βουλόμενος τὰ μέλλοντα, καὶ τοὺς ἀθλητὰς τῆς εὐσεβείας ἐπιῤῥῶσαι θέλων. Νῦν μὲν γὰρ διὰ τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ χάριν πολλῆς ἀπολαύομεν τῆς εἰρήνης· καὶ γὰρ βασιλεῖς ἐν εὐσεβείᾳ ζῶσι, καὶ ἄρχοντες τὴν ἀλήθειαν ἐπέγνωσαν, καὶ δῆμοι καὶ πόλεις καὶ ἔθνη τῆς πλάνης ἀπαλλαγέντες, τὸν Χριστὸν ἅπαντες προσκυνοῦσι· τότε δὲ ἐν ἀρχῇ τοῦ κηρύγματος, ἄρτι τῶν σπερμάτων τῆς εὐσεβείας καταβαλλομένων, πολὺς ὁ πόλεμος καὶ διάφορος καὶ ποικίλος. Καὶ γὰρ ἄρχοντες καὶ βασιλεῖς καὶ οἰκεῖοι καὶ συγγενεῖς καὶ πάντες τοῖς πιστοῖς ἐπολέμουν, καὶ διὰ τῆς φύσεως αὐτῆς ὁ πόλεμος ᾔρετο. Καὶ γὰρ πατὴρ τέκνον παρέδωκε πολλάκις, καὶ θυγατέρα μήτηρ, καὶ οἰκέτην δεσπότης.
thought_title: Present contest, future crowns; the wicked's brief luxury and the resurrection hope
orientation: Chrysostom is addressing his congregation, urging them to judge God's providence not from present circumstances alone but from the future, and then he introduces Paul's repeated teaching on the resurrection.
pass_a_gloss: Let us not therefore vote about the providence of God from present things only, but also from future things. For present things are a contest and wrestling-grounds and a stadium, but future things are prizes and crowns and awards. Just as therefore the athlete must fight in the wrestling-ground and in sweat and dust and much heat and labors and hardships, so also the righteous man must here endure many things and bear all things nobly, if indeed he is going to receive back bright crowns there. But if the prosperities of the wicked trouble some people, let them also reckon again about these people that, just as robbers and grave-diggers and murderers and pirates sailing the sea, before entering the law-court, enjoy much luxury, making the misfortunes of others their own wealth, and acquiring unjust wealth, and getting drunk every day; but whenever they come under the votes of the judge, they pay the penalty for all those things; so also these people who buy prostitutes, and set out Sybaritic tables, and raise their eyebrows, and swagger in the marketplace, and tear the poor to pieces, when the only-begotten Son of God arrives with his angels, and sits on that judgment seat, and brings the inhabited world into the middle, having been brought in naked and bereft of all their show, and having no advocate nor protector, without any pardon they will be carried away into the rivers of fire. Do not therefore bless these people because of the luxury here, but weep because of the coming punishment; nor call the righteous man wretched because of the poverty here, but bless him because of the coming wealth of good things, and root the word about the resurrection in your own mind, so that, if you are good and are tested, you may become more approved, taking on greater eagerness by the future hopes; and if you are bad, you may stand away from wickedness, making yourself more temperate by the fear of the coming punishment. Section 2. For this reason Paul also constantly sets in motion for us the word about the resurrection, just as indeed also today you heard him crying out and saying: For we know that if our earthly dwelling of the tent is dissolved, we have a dwelling from God not made by hands, eternal, in the heavens. But rather let us lead the word up higher, and let us see from where he fell into the word about the resurrection. For not simply, nor as it happened, does he constantly set in motion this teaching; but at once wishing to teach the future things, and wanting to strengthen the athletes of piety. For now through the grace of God we enjoy much peace; for kings live in piety, and rulers have recognized the truth, and peoples and cities and nations, having been freed from error, all worship Christ; but then at the beginning of the preaching, when the seeds of piety were just being sown, the war was great and varied and manifold. For rulers and kings and household members and relatives and all made war on the faithful, and through nature itself the war was stirred up. For a father handed over a child often, and a mother a daughter, and a master a household servant.

choices.why: The verb ψηφίζομαι means to vote or decide by casting a vote; keeping 'vote' preserves the judicial metaphor that runs through the passage (judge's votes, judgment seat).
σκάμμα is the dug-up area where wrestlers competed; 'wrestling-grounds' keeps the athletic specificity alongside 'stadium'.
The compound ἀπολαμβάνω means to receive back what is due; 'receive back' preserves the sense of recompense for labors.
The word means those who dig up tombs to rob them; 'grave-diggers' is literal and keeps the criminal list vivid.
The idiom means to put on haughty airs; rendering it literally preserves the bodily gesture Chrysostom names.
The aorist imperative of ῥιζόω means to cause to take root; 'root' as a verb keeps the agricultural metaphor and the command's force.

pass_b_english: So let us not judge God's providence from present things alone, but also from the things to come. For the present things are a contest, wrestling-grounds, and a stadium; the things to come are prizes, crowns, and awards. Just as an athlete must fight in the wrestling-ground with sweat, dust, great heat, labors, and hardships, so also the righteous person here must endure many things and bear everything nobly, if he is going to receive back the shining crowns there. But if the prosperity of the wicked troubles some people, let them reason about those people in the same way again: just as robbers, grave-diggers, murderers, and pirates who sail the sea enjoy great luxury before they enter the courtroom, making other people's misfortunes their own wealth, acquiring unjust riches, and getting drunk every day—but when they come under the judge's votes, they pay the penalty for all those things—so also these people who buy prostitutes, set out Sybaritic tables, raise their eyebrows, swagger in the marketplace, and tear the poor to pieces, when the only-begotten Son of God arrives with His own angels and sits on that judgment seat and brings the whole world into the middle, will be brought in naked and stripped of all their show, with no advocate or protector, and without any pardon they will be carried away into the rivers of fire. So do not call these people blessed because of their luxury here, but weep for them because of the punishment to come. And do not call the righteous person wretched because of his poverty here, but call him blessed because of the coming wealth of good things. Root the teaching about the resurrection in your own mind, so that if you are good and are tested, you may become more approved, receiving greater eagerness from the hopes to come; and if you are wicked, you may turn away from evil, making yourself more self-controlled by the fear of the coming punishment.

2. For this reason Paul constantly stirs up the teaching about the resurrection for us, just as you heard him crying out today and saying: "For we know that if our earthly dwelling of the tent is destroyed, we have a dwelling from God, not made by hands, eternal, in the heavens" (2 Corinthians 5:1). But let us take the discussion further back and see from where he fell into the teaching about the resurrection. For he does not stir up this teaching constantly simply or by chance, but because he wants at the same time to teach about the things to come and to strengthen the athletes of godliness. For now, by God's grace, we enjoy great peace: kings live in godliness, rulers have come to know the truth, and peoples, cities, and nations have been freed from error and all worship Christ. But then, at the beginning of the preaching, when the seeds of godliness had just been sown, the war was great, varied, and of many kinds. For rulers, kings, household members, relatives, and everyone made war on the faithful, and the war was stirred up through nature itself. For a father often handed over his child, a mother her daughter, and a master his servant.

problems.source_quote: ψηφισώμεθα περὶ τῆς τοῦ Θεοῦ προνοίας
problems.why: ψηφίζομαι means 'judge/decide,' not 'vote'; 'vote' implies democratic process absent in source.

problems.source_quote: ἡ ἐπίγειος ἡμῶν οἰκία τοῦ σκήνους
problems.why: Greek has 'dwelling of the tent,' not 'tent dwelling'; 'tent' modifies 'dwelling' as genitive of apposition or epexegetical genitive.
problems.fix: our earthly dwelling of the tent

problems.quote: when the only-begotten Son of God arrives
problems.source_quote: ὅταν ὁ μονογενὴς Υἱὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ παραγένηται μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν ἑαυτοῦ
problems.why: Missing 'with his own angels' (μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν ἑαυτοῦ), important for judicial scene.
problems.fix: when the only-begotten Son of God arrives with his own angels
problems.ruling: Source has 'μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν ἑαυτοῦ' ('with His own angels'); English omits this phrase, losing meaning.

edits.new: our earthly dwelling of the tent

edits.old: when the only-begotten Son of God arrives with His angels
edits.new: when the only-begotten Son of God arrives with His own angels

ἡ ἐπίγειος ἡμῶν οἰκία τοῦ σκήνους is 'earthly dwelling of the tent,' not 'tent dwelling'; changed to 'our earthly dwelling of the tent'.
μετὰ τῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν ἑαυτοῦ means 'with his own angels'; added 'own' to 'with His own angels'.

problems.quote: the war was stirred up through nature itself
problems.source_quote: διὰ τῆς φύσεως αὐτῆς ὁ πόλεμος ᾔρετο
problems.why: φύσις here means 'natural affection/family ties,' not 'nature itself'; war arose through family bonds betrayed.
problems.fix: the war was stirred up through natural affection itself
problems.ruling: Context: fathers betray children, masters servants. φύσις = natural kinship bonds, not 'nature itself'; 'through nature itself' misleads readers.

edits.old: the war was stirred up through nature itself
edits.new: the war was stirred up through natural affection itself

fixed: Changed 'nature itself' to 'natural affection itself' because φύσις here refers to natural family affection, not nature in general.

problems.quote: and the war was stirred up through natural affection itself
problems.source_quote: διὰ τῆς φύσεως αὐτῆς ὁ πόλεμος ᾔρετο
problems.why: φύσις here means 'nature' broadly, not 'natural affection' specifically; the war was stirred up 'through nature itself.'
problems.fix: and the war was stirred up through nature itself
problems.ruling: φύσις here means 'nature' broadly; 'natural affection' (φιλοστοργία) misleads—context shows family members betraying each other, not through affection but despite/because of natural ties.

last_rejected.why: 'fell into' suggests accident; ἐνέπεσεν here means 'came to', 'arrived at', or 'launched into' the topic.
last_rejected.fix: see where he came to the teaching about the resurrection
